newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: SAirGroup dives into 497 mln Sfr loss.
newsitem.headline: SAirGroup dives into 497 mln Sfr loss.

text.p: SAirGroup, the newly created holding company that includes the Swissair airline, said its operating profit in 1996 rose 40 percent, but provisions and the write-down of its stake in Sabena pushed the group into a new loss of 497 million Swiss francs.
SAirGroup said in a statement that in light of this result it did not plan to pay any dividend.
SAirGroup last paid a dividend on its 1992 accounts.
The statement was issued after a meeting of SAirGroup's board of directors.
SAirGroup's operating profit rose to 344 million francs in 1996 from a restated 247 million.
SAirGroup's results were for the first time calculated according to International Accounting Standards (IAS), but the group did not restate all its 1995 results.
In 1995 SAirGroup, which then was known as Swissair Group, had an operating profit of 237 million francs and a net loss of 147 million, including extraordinary charges of 365 million.
SAirGroup's cash flow amounted to 873 million francs in 1996, but the company did not give a restated comparison.
Operating revenue rose to 8,212 million francs from 7,028 million.
However, SAirGroup also said it took provisions of 300 million francs for "future structural adjustment to the full liberalisation of the European air transport market from April 1, 1997."
A company spokesman said details of what this 300 million francs would cover was not available, but the company would provide further information at its news conference on April 18.

"While resulting in a sizable loss for the year, these provisions should lay a sound foundation for further enhancing the SAirGroup's ability to compete in the newly-liberalised European air transport market," SAirGroup said.
Restructuring charges in 1995 were taken to cover the cost of cutting SAirGroup's workforce by 2,000 jobs. Some 1,200 of these cuts already took effect in 1996.
The spokesman declined to say whether further job cuts were planned.
